messages:
marta: heads up — after last night's BMC rolling update in eu-west-1 we started seeing OOB flakiness on rack p3. 8 nodes lost SSH to host, but IPMI responds intermittently and we have duplicated MACs on the OOB VLAN so provisioning fails. provisioning jobs timeout.

ben: which BMC image was rolled? any change to EEPROM/asset scripts?

marta: image v2.14.0 -> v2.15.1 (vendor). release notes mentioned 'IPMI stack improvements' but not MAC behaviour. attached quick dump from a box: 

```
# ipmitool lan print 1
MAC Address              : 00:11:22:33:44:55
IP Address Source        : DHCP Address
Subnet Mask              : 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway IP       : 10.0.0.1
DHCP Enabled             : Yes

# on another node in same rack
MAC Address              : 00:11:22:33:44:55
...
```

marta: nodes sometimes show secureboot=disabled in UEFI var, then flip back to enabled after a BMC heartbeat. serial consoles show UEFI errors on NVMe init briefly.

oncall-bot: Scheduled: bmc-rolling-upgrade-eu-west (ID 2026-03-16T02:00Z) — origin: infra-release-pipeline

kai: this sounds like a DHCP / ARP collision on OOB network after BMC reboots. vendor firmware might be falling back to a default MAC when NIC reset races with IPMI stack. we should isolate OOB VLAN for the rack and disable DHCP so nodes don't grab unexpected IPs while we investigate.

ben: agree. short list:
- isolate VLAN on switch (move p3 to maintenance vlan)
- power-cycle BMCs one at a time with 5m gap (avoid mass reboot)
- check serial console for UEFI secureboot flag flips
- if duplicated MAC present, force a BMC factory-reset on that unit and re-provision MAC via vendor tooling

marta: trying isolation now. datacenter-ops can you put rack p3 on vlan 600-maint? need minimal impact window.

datacenter-ops: done — rack p3 moved to vlan 600-maint, OOB network isolated. PV traffic now routed off the main OOB fabric.

olivia: tagging product: this impacts Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1. we've lost 8 x A100 equivalents from the pool; autoscaler rebalanced but 3 customer pods were descheduled. customers on reserved capacity might see degraded throughput. estimate 12% capacity hit for that AZ.

ben: do we have a revert plan for v2.15.1? vendor previously had a known issue with MAC assignment in v2.13. they fixed it then reintroduced in this patch. rollback path: vendor web tool or BMC recovery image flash via USB. flashing at scale is painful.

kai: if factory reset is required, we should canary with 1 node and validate provisioning end-to-end (PXE, IPMI, SSH). we must avoid toggling secureboot across many hosts simultaneously. Also consider enabling IPMI MAC pinning in the switch (static ARP) for affected ports.

marta: canary started on p3-04 (serial active). logs show UEFI variable nvram write error then secureboot remains enabled after factory reset. provisioning job succeeded for that node after re-provision.

ben: good. what's the ETA to remediate the other 7? we should script vendor flash for the ones that fail factory-reset.

marta: manual factory-reset + quick re-provision ~18m/node. with team we can do parallel 3 at a time => ~50m. vendor script might cut that to 6m/node but need vendor auth.

olivia: ops/business note — if this drifts to other racks in eu-west, we need to consider moving some dedicated workloads to us-east temporarily. cost to cross-AZ traffic and transient redistribution ~estimated $800/day if we sustain that for 3 days. raising to leadership if remediation stretches.

datacenter-ops: physical status: no thermal alarms. ambient temps normal. we did notice BMC power cycling during the roll at ~03:12Z (correlates to infra pipeline).

kai: mitigation checklist I'm executing:
- [x] isolate VLAN
- [x] canary factory-reset p3-04
- [x] verify provisioning and kernel boot
- [ ] schedule phased resets for remaining nodes (3 in parallel)
- [ ] vendor escalation opened (case# 20260316-73)

marta: creating incident ticket and runbook note. copying the minimal commands we used in case others need to replicate: 

```
# activate serial over lan
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS sol activate
# soft reset BMC
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS mc reset cold
# factory reset (vendor CLI)
vendor-bmc-cli --host $BMC --factory-reset --confirm
# reflash recovery image (if needed)
vendor-bmc-flash --image recovery.img --target $BMC
```

ben: please add explicit cleanup: update DHCP lease database, clear stale ARP entries on edge switches (clear mac address-table dynamic vlan 600). also add ephemeral host tags to avoid routing jobs to 'maintenance' rack.

marta: done. I've added the steps to the incident doc and set a follow-up for post-incident eval.

olivia: pinging sales/support to pre-empt customers with dedicated capacity impacted — small batch email + status page note.

datacenter-ops: executing phased resets now (p3-01, p3-02, p3-03). will report each success.

marta: thanks all — will update thread as nodes come back. plan is to hold the rest of the BMC roll until vendor provides a patched image with MAC handling fix or we validate safe rollback process.

ben: once stabilized let's run a quick script to scan OOB fabric for MAC duplication across racks to avoid recurrence.

kai: agreed. also add a prom alert for sudden MAC churn on OOB VLANs.

marta: p3-01 back and provisioned. p3-02 back too. p3-03 showing SAS LED error but host is up; manual NVMe reseat scheduled.

olivia: capacity back to 92% for AZ. will continue to monitor. filing cost/impact notes for finance.

marta: closing for now — I'll attach the incident ID in the postmortem once it's created. :thumbsup:
